questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \quad \Delta H=-94 \mathrm{kcal} \\ & 2 \mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \Delta H=-135.2 \mathrm{kcal}\end{aligned}$
The heat of formation of $\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$ is :
questions.solution:
The required reaction is $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g) & \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}(g) \\ \mathrm{CO}_2(g) & \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g)\end{aligned}\Delta H=\frac{+135.2}{2} \mathrm{kcal}$...(i) $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{ g}) & \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{ g})\end{aligned}\Delta H =-94 \mathrm{kcal}$...(ii)
The required equation is come out by adding Eq. (i) and (ii) So, $\Delta H_{f(\mathrm{CO})}=-94+\frac{135.2}{2}=-26.4 \mathrm{kcal}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy change for the transition of liquid water to steam is $40.8 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ at 373 K. Calculate the entropy of vaporisation of water.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta S_{\text{vap }}=\frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap }}}{T} \\ & \because \Delta H_{\text{vap }}=40.8 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}, T=373 \mathrm{ K} \\ & \Delta S_{\text{vap }}=\frac{40.8 \times 10^3}{373}=109.4 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Enthalpy is equal to
questions.solution:
The Gibbs-Helmholtz equation is as
$G=H+T\left[\frac{\delta G}{\delta T}\right]_p$
Dividing above equation by $T^2\frac{G}{T^2}=\frac{H}{T^2}+\frac{1}{T}\left[\frac{\delta G}{\delta T}\right]_p$
This on rearrangement becomes.
$\left[\frac{\delta(G / T)}{\delta T}\right]=-\frac{H}{T^2}$
Thus, enthalpy, $H=-T^2\left[\frac{\delta G / T}{\delta T}\right]_p$
Where, $\quad H=$ enthalpy

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Following method of extracting Zn is based on thermodynamics
$A: 2 \mathrm{ZnS}+3 \mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{ZnO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_2B: \mathrm{ZnO}+\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{CO}$
If $\Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}$ (standard free energies of formation, in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of $\mathrm{ZnS}=-205.4,
\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{ZnO}=-318.0, \mathrm{SO}_2=-300.4 \\ & \mathrm{CO}=-137.3\end{aligned}$
Free energy changes of the above reaction $A and B$ (respectively) will be
questions.solution:
For reaction $A\begin{aligned} \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} & =2 \Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{ZnO})+2 \Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}\left(\mathrm{SO}_2\right)-2 G_f^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{ZnS}) \\ & =2[-3182-300.4+205.4] \\ & =-826.4 \mathrm{ kJ} \quad\left(\Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{ element })=0\right)\end{aligned}$
For reaction $B\begin{aligned} \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} & =\Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{CO})-\Delta G_f^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{ZnO}) \\ & =-137.3+328.2 \\ & =+180.9 \mathrm{ kJ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ice melts into water, the entropy
questions.solution:
Entropy is the measure of randomness. In liquids randomness is more than solids.
$\because$ When ice melts, randomness increases, (solid $\longrightarrow$ liquid)
$\therefore$ Entropy increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One mole of ice is converted into water at 273 K. The entropies of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(s)$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(t)$ are 38.20 and $\quad 60.01 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}$ respectively. The enthalpy change for the conversion is
questions.solution:
$\because \quad \Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$
At equilibrium, $\Delta G=0\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \Delta H & =T \Delta S \\
\Delta H & =273 \times(60.01-38.20) \\
& =5954.13 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}=5.954 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1} \\
& \approx 6 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
